commits.edited_message:
Reject shrink requests in extend_to_size_with_zero (GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff)

heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() forwarded its target width/height
unchecked to HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero(), which only ever grows
an image. On a target smaller than the current plane size, the right-edge fill
length (subsampled_width - old_width) underflowed uint32_t and the memset wrote
past the end of the pixel plane.

Reject a target smaller than the current size up front with a usage error, and
short-circuit when the size is unchanged. As defense in depth, add a per-plane
preflight that rejects, before modifying any plane, a target that would map a
plane to a smaller extent than its current logical size implies, so a rejected
request cannot leave the image partially modified. Document the precondition on
the C API and add regression tests covering the shrink, grow, and unchanged
cases.

The overflow is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract (shrinking) size; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it, and both
in-tree callers (extract_image_area, heif-enc tiling) only ever grow.

(cherry picked from commit bbbbc3c33dc05da1e68b2b3357fa1d04e6fe9501)

Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane (issue #1796)

A Cb/Cr plane must cover at least the chroma-subsampled size (round_up) of the
logical image, the extent has_standard_plane_sizes() and check_plane_layout()
treat as the plane. Nothing stopped a caller from building an undersized Cb/Cr
plane through the public API (heif_image_create() + heif_image_add_plane()), and
an undersized colour plane is a memory-safety hazard: it caused out-of-bounds
reads during RGB conversion (issue #1796) because the converter reads each plane
at the size the logical dimensions imply.

Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane in add_channel() so such an image can never be
built. An oversized plane is left acceptable: the conversion operators read each
plane only at the extent the layout implies, and extend_to_size_with_zero()
already rejects a target that would shrink any plane before its per-row fill runs
(the per-plane preflight added for GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff), so an oversized plane
cannot underflow that fill. Only Cb/Cr are constrained; alpha, depth and other
auxiliary planes may keep a size that differs from the colour planes.

All internal producers (decoders, colour-conversion operators, the uncompressed
codec, the internal convert path) already compute Cb/Cr with round_up, so none
are affected. A new add_channel_checks covers the accept/reject cases directly;
the downstream-guard tests keep building an oversized plane to exercise the
check_plane_layout() and per-tile encoder guards, which still catch it.

This is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract image; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it.

(cherry picked from commit ff7bf3ce4e63c911d2f769164250bdb653dcb547)

coupling:
The reachable out-of-bounds write (the per-row right-edge fill in HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero() computing its memset length as (subsampled_width - old_width), which underflows uint32_t when a chroma plane is larger than its target subsampled extent) is closed in the real batch by TWO independent guards introduced across two commits, and each edited commit silently defers the oversized-Cb/Cr case to the other, so no single diff looks wrong.

Commit A = 'Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane (issue #1796)' (real d2ba4ba). Real d2ba4ba rejected ANY mismatched Cb/Cr plane in add_channel() with `width != expected || height != expected`, which blocks building the oversized plane at all. My edit relaxes it to `width < expected || height < expected` -- rejecting only an UNDERSIZED plane (the genuine issue #1796 OOB-read), and accepting an oversized one. Read alone this is correct, self-consistent maintenance: it fixes #1796, and its comment/commit-message correctly observe that an oversized plane cannot underflow the extend fill BECAUSE extend_to_size_with_zero() has a per-plane preflight that rejects a shrinking plane (commit B). Nothing in this diff is wrong on its own.

Commit B = 'Reject shrink requests in extend_to_size_with_zero' (real 5eddd08). Real 5eddd08 added only the whole-image logical guard. My edit adds the per-plane preflight that commit A relies on -- but it compares each plane's NEW subsampled target against the plane's OLD subsampled target derived from the logical image size (get_subsampled_size(m_width,...) vs get_subsampled_size(width,...)), NOT against the plane's actual stored size (component.m_width). For every consistent image old_sub == component.m_width, so the preflight is indistinguishable from the correct one and passes all normal inputs. It therefore never notices an individually OVERSIZED chroma plane (component.m_width > old_sub). Read alone this is a thorough, plausible 'no plane may shrink' guard.

Composition: commit A accepts the oversized Cb/Cr plane, trusting commit B's preflight to catch it; commit B's preflight measures against the logical-derived extent and so does not catch it. The oversized plane reaches the fill loop, old_width(60) > subsampled_width(51), and (51-60) underflows to ~4 GB -> OOB write.

Why a correct fix is non-local: the defect is the SHARED FALSE ASSUMPTION spanning the two commits -- commit A's comment asserts the extend preflight rejects oversized planes, which is only true of the plane's actual size, while commit B's preflight was written against the logical-derived size. Neither diff, reviewed in isolation, exhibits a defect: A correctly fixes #1796 and correctly describes B as the backstop; B is a correct-looking per-plane shrink guard. A reviewer must correlate the two commits -- noticing that the extent B actually checks is not the extent A depends on -- to see the bug, and the repair must reconcile them (either re-tighten A's add_channel to reject oversized, or change B's preflight to measure component.m_width). On the base tree neither guard exists, so the same public-API sequence already fires (incomplete_fix): the edited batch ships an incomplete fix for this GHSA-j2rv/GHSA-hqc2 plane-size class.
